S36.01.needs: a Free account or a paid account; a question that triggers web search
S36.01.note: The code does not show which question triggers web search, so the tester must find one that does.
steps: Sign in and open a chat.
Send a question that makes the answer search the web for current facts.
Look for small rounded pill chips with a site name placed right after a sentence in the answer.
Compare with Expected: claims should carry an inline marker naming the source.
S36.01.where: In a chat answer that searched the web: small pill chips showing a site name sit at the end of claims. Each chip's accessible name reads "Source {{indices}}: {{sites}}".

steps: Open a chat answer that used web sources.
Hover the book icon under the answer and click "Show sources".
In the panel on the right, look at the bold first line of each source row.
Compare with Expected: each cited source shows its title.
S36.02.where: Chat answer > "Show sources" button under the answer (tooltip "Sources") > Research panel tab "Sources".

S36.03.note: The shown domain is the publisher's, not the search router's, per the code comments.
steps: Open a chat answer that used web sources.
Click "Show sources".
Read the grey line under each source title; it shows the site domain.
Hover a site-name pill in the answer to see the same info in the tooltip.
Compare with Expected: each source names its publisher or site.
S36.03.where: Chat answer > "Show sources" button under the answer > Research panel tab "Sources" (the grey line under each source title).

S36.04.needs: a web-search answer; a browser with internet access
steps: Open a chat answer that used web sources and click "Show sources".
Click one source row.
Look for a new browser tab opening the source page.
Compare with Expected: the source opens from its row.
S36.04.where: Chat answer > "Show sources" button > Research panel tab "Sources" > click a source row.

S36.05.needs: a web-search answer; the date only appears when the source provides one
S36.05.note: The date is shown only when the source provides one, so an answer may show none.
steps: Open a chat answer that used web sources and click "Show sources".
Look at the grey line under a source title for a date.
If there is no date, check the "Report" tab on a Deep Research report.
Compare with Expected: cited sources show a publication date when the source has one.
S36.05.where: Chat answer > "Show sources" button > Research panel tab "Sources" (source row text); also the "Report" tab > Sources list.

steps: Open a chat answer that used web sources and click "Show sources".
Read the grey line under a source title.
Look for "Retrieved" followed by a date.
Compare with Expected: each source shows when it was retrieved.
S36.06.where: Chat answer > "Show sources" button > Research panel tab "Sources" (grey line under a source title).

labels.text: Project files used in this answer

S36.07.needs: a web-search answer; a project with an uploaded file for the file icon; past chats for the chat icon
S36.07.note: The icons have no visible text, so the tester confirms them by sight; the code shows a globe, a file and a chat icon.
steps: Open a chat answer that used web sources and look at the small globe icon in the site-name pill.
Open a chat answer that cited a project file (see S36.09) and look for the file icon.
Open a chat answer that used past chats (see S36.14) and look for the chat icon.
Compare with Expected: each source type has its own icon.
S36.07.where: Chat answer: source chips show a globe icon for web sources; project files show a file icon in the group "Project files used in this answer"; past chats show a chat icon in the group "Previous chats this answer used".

S36.08.note: The code shows the source snippet, trimmed to 180 characters, but does not mark it as a quote, so the tester judges that by reading.
steps: Open a chat answer that used web sources.
Hover a site-name pill in the answer and read the tooltip.
Click "Show sources" and read the short text under a source title.
Compare with Expected: each cited source shows a quoted excerpt supporting the claim.
S36.08.where: Chat answer > hover a site-name pill (tooltip) or > "Show sources" > Research panel tab "Sources" (text under the source title).

labels.text: Project files used in this answer

S36.09.needs: a project with an uploaded multi-page PDF; a Free or paid account
S36.09.note: The page label comes from formatProjectFileAnchor, which shows "p. N"; the preview-at-page behaviour is read from the URL in SourcesPanel.tsx.
steps: Open a project that has an uploaded PDF and ask a question that answers from it.
In the answer, find the group of chips "Project files used in this answer".
Read the chip that shows the file name and "p." followed by a number.
Click the chip and look whether the file preview opens on that page.
Compare with Expected: the citation names the page and opens the file there.
S36.09.where: Chat answer > group "Project files used in this answer" > click a file chip showing "p. N" > the project file preview opens on that page.

S36.14.needs: two chats in the same account; the answer must draw on the earlier one
S36.14.note: The code shows the chip links to the chat with a message highlight parameter; the highlight is confirmed only by sight.
steps: Have a chat where the assistant recalls an earlier conversation.
Ask a question that makes the answer draw on that earlier chat.
Find the group "Previous chats this answer used" under the answer.
Click one chip and look for the earlier chat opening with that message highlighted.
Compare with Expected: the citation opens the exact message.
S36.14.where: Chat answer that used past chats > group "Previous chats this answer used" > click a chip (opens the earlier chat at that message).

steps: Open a chat answer that used web sources.
Read each sentence and find the small pill chip placed right after it.
Hover the chip to see which source it names.
Compare with Expected: each chip sits at the claim it supports.
S36.16.where: Chat answer: the source chip sits right after the sentence it supports (site-name pill).

S36.17.needs: a web-search answer where one claim cites several sources
S36.17.note: A multi-source claim is needed to see the +N chip; the code does not control how often it appears.
steps: Open a chat answer that used web sources.
Look for a site-name chip showing "+" and a number.
Hover the chip and read the tooltip list.
Compare with Expected: all sources for the claim are visible.
S36.17.where: Chat answer: a chip with "+N" after the site name; hover it to see all sources for that claim.

labels.text: This report refers to {{count}} numbered sources, but the run recorded no links for them.

S36.19.needs: a report whose run recorded no source links but whose text has numbered references
S36.19.note: The code shows this notice only for a report with no captured links; a single broken link has no notice, so a tester may not find one.
steps: Open a Deep Research report from the Research panel's "Report" tab.
Scroll to the end of the report body.
Look for the "Sources" heading and the sentence about numbered sources.
Compare with Expected: when a source cannot be opened, the product says so rather than showing a dead link.
S36.19.where: Chat > Deep research report > "Report" tab in the Research panel > bottom of the report, section "Sources".

S36.25.needs: a completed Deep Research report with sources
S36.25.note: The export buttons are labelled Markdown, PDF and Word in the code; the tester checks the saved file's citations by reading it.
steps: Open a Deep Research report from the Research panel's "Report" tab.
Click the export button "Markdown" (or "PDF" or "Word").
Open the downloaded file.
Compare with Expected: the citations and the source list are present in the exported file.
S36.25.where: Chat > Deep research report > "Report" tab in the Research panel > export buttons "Markdown", "PDF" and "Word" in the report header.
